investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence of orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was collected, confirming the agent VM never reached a schedulable state within the eval window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but had no remaining capacity at the time of the eval run (evidenced by "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules ("4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector"). Preemption was also unavailable ("0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling"). Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received the orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence required by the expected-output contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence of orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was collected, confirming the agent VM never reached a schedulable state within the eval window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but had no remaining capacity at the time of the eval run (evidenced by "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules ("4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector"). Preemption was also unavailable ("0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling"). Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received the orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence required by the expected-output contract. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster are configured to support kata peer-pods, which creates a narrow scheduling target; if those 2 nodes are at capacity simultaneously, all remote agent creation attempts will fail.
[Possible] Leaked or stuck remote agent VMs from prior eval runs or user workloads consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

[Lower confidence] A quota or limit range applied to the eval service account or namespace that caps the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm resources requestable, causing the scheduler to report insufficient capacity even if node-level slots exist.
